resources.string: LyricCast puts song lyrics on a big screen. Build a library, arrange songs into setlists, and present them to a TV or to other devices — no dedicated hardware needed.
Import an OpenSong archive or a LyricCast backup to get started in seconds, or write songs yourself. Categories keep a large library manageable.
A setlist is an ordered run of songs for one service or event. Prepare it ahead of time, then present it start to finish without hunting for the next song.
Send lyrics to any Google Cast device on the same Wi-Fi network. The Cast icon appears in the top bar once a receiver is found.
No Cast device? Start a session and let other phones or tablets nearby follow along in sync — one device leads, the rest keep up automatically.
During a service, step through verses, blank the screen between songs, and follow along. Colours, font size and blank-on-start all live in Settings.
Your library lives here. Songs holds everything you have added; Setlists holds the running orders you build from them.
Write a song from scratch, or build a setlist by picking songs from your library and putting them in order.
Import is the fastest way to fill the app — it reads OpenSong archives and LyricCast backups. Export saves your work to a file. Deleted items also live here, so an accidental delete is easy to undo.
Create colour-coded categories and assign them to songs so a large library stays searchable.
Presentation colours, font size, theme and session defaults.
The Cast icon appears in the top bar whenever a Google Cast device is on the same Wi-Fi network. Tap it to put lyrics on the TV.

Start a session here to make this device the presenter — other nearby devices running LyricCast can follow whatever you show, without needing their own copy of your songs. To follow someone else instead, use the Join session tab.
The title is what you will search for later, so make it recognisable. The lyrics go in the field below — each block becomes one screen when you present.
Set the order in which verses and choruses are shown, including repeats — no need to duplicate the text.
Saving adds the song to your library; leaving without saving discards it. Assigning a category first makes the song easier to find once the library grows.
Something you will recognise later — a date or an event name works well.
Pick songs from your library, then drag them into the order you want. This list is empty until you have added some songs.
Background colour, font colour and maximum font size control what appears on the TV or the following device.
With this on, the screen stays empty when you open a song, so nothing appears before you are ready.
